articles.title: The Latest: Trump highlights his own record at midterm Republican convention
articles.description: Republicans are gathering in Dallas for a unique two-day midterm convention, focusing on President Donald Trump. Trump plans to speak both nights and Vice President JD Vance will also address attendees. The event aims to boost Republican candidates by highlighting Trump's first two years in office. Trump believes running on his record is the GOP's best strategy despite low approval ratings. Meanwhile, Democrats are planning counterprogramming. Trump has commented on high oil prices due to the Iran war, suggesting they won't drop until after the midterms. The war, now in its seventh month, has been widely criticized.

articles.title: Oil Price Today (September 10): Crude oil at $101 as Iran attack on 10 ships raises supply fears. $120 in sight?
articles.description: On Thursday, oil prices surged above one hundred dollars per barrel as traders evaluated the risks associated with supply disruptions stemming from recent shipping attacks. Iran has claimed responsibility for targeting ten vessels after the United States destroyed five tankers. Market analysts warn that if tensions continue in the contested Strait of Hormuz, oil prices could escalate further, potentially reaching one hundred twenty dollars per barrel.

articles.title: Currency markets subdued as oil shock lifts global yields; ECB, U.S. inflation eyed
articles.description: Currency markets remained steady as investors assessed rising oil prices and bond yields. The Japanese yen's strong rally paused before key United States inflation readings were released. Global bond yields climbed higher, reaching their highest levels since last year due to energy pressures. Central banks in Europe and Japan are expected to raise interest rates soon. United States inflation data will guide the Federal Reserve's upcoming policy decisions.

articles.title: Brent holds above $100 as tanker attacks deepen supply fear
articles.description: Oil prices are holding steady as Brent crude exceeds one hundred dollars per barrel. Traders are anticipating further supply interruptions due to recent assaults on shipping. In response, Iran claimed it targeted ten vessels following the U.S. sinking five Iranian oil tankers. This back-and-forth suggests continued disruptions in the Persian Gulf. Furthermore, global stockpiles are dwindling, prompting an increase in oil price projections.
